messages.author: alice
messages.content: hey team, we need to do the SLO threshold review I mentioned. we've been getting false-positive pages and the current thresholds are wrong

messages.author: alice
messages.content: current code has: critical if error_rate > 0.10 or budget > 95%. this missed real incidents last month

messages.author: bob
messages.content: yeah I got paged 3 times last week and each time the service was actually fine. the 0.10 threshold is too high

messages.author: carol
messages.content: agreed. we had a real incident where error rate was 0.07 and we didn't get paged in time because threshold was 0.10

messages.author: dave
messages.content: also the budget threshold at 95% is way too late - by the time we're at 95% consumed we're already in trouble

messages.author: frank
messages.content: I think we should keep 0.10 as the threshold to avoid alert fatigue. lowering it will just mean more false positives

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Q3 error budget summary posted in wiki

messages.author: alice
messages.content: frank - actually the opposite is happening. 0.10 is causing us to MISS incidents, not over-page. we need to go lower

messages.author: frank
messages.content: fair point, but what about the noise? we'll get paged for every little blip

messages.author: alice
messages.content: that's what the warning level is for. we're not removing thresholds, we're adding nuance

messages.author: carol
messages.content: so we need: critical threshold, warning threshold, and a paging condition that considers latency

messages.author: erin
messages.content: what's the proposal for critical error rate threshold?

messages.author: dave
messages.content: I propose 0.05 - that way we catch the incidents we were missing but still filter out genuine noise below 5%

messages.author: bob
messages.content: 0.05 sounds right to me. that's the industry standard for SLO alerting

messages.author: carol
messages.content: agreed on 0.05 for critical error rate

messages.author: alice
messages.content: quick note: we should use >= 0.05, not > 0.05 — we want to catch exactly-at-threshold too

messages.author: frank
messages.content: why does the >= vs > distinction matter here?

messages.author: alice
messages.content: because > 0.05 would miss a service running at exactly 5.0% error rate. >= catches it. this is important for the boundary cases in our SLO contract

messages.author: dave
messages.content: good call. so: status = critical if error_rate >= 0.05

messages.author: bob
messages.content: now for budget threshold - what percentage budget consumed should trigger critical?

messages.author: carol
messages.content: I was going to propose 95% but thinking about it more, that's too late. by 95% we've almost no budget left

messages.author: alice
messages.content: exactly. 90% is the right threshold for critical budget. gives us time to react before we're completely burned out

messages.author: carol
messages.content: right, 95% is too late. I'm changing my proposal to 90%

messages.author: dave
messages.content: 90% makes sense. critical if budget_consumed_pct > 90

messages.author: alice
messages.content: agreed. critical: error_rate >= 0.05 OR budget_consumed_pct > 90

messages.author: frank
messages.content: what about warning? we should have a lower threshold to catch degrading services before they hit critical

messages.author: erin
messages.content: what error rate for warning?

messages.author: bob
messages.content: I propose 0.02 - anything above 2% is worth watching

messages.author: niaj
messages.content: 2% seems too aggressive, we'll get warning spam

messages.author: carol
messages.content: yeah I think 0.02 might be a bit tight. what about splitting the difference?

messages.author: alice
messages.content: let's look at our historical data... checking grafana

messages.author: alice
messages.content: ok so we have services that routinely hit 1.5% during normal load. we don't want to warn on those

messages.author: bob
messages.content: so what threshold won't catch normal noise?

messages.author: dave
messages.content: what if we go with 0.01? that's 1% error rate. our normal range is 0.1-0.8%, so 1% would catch real degradation
